Healthy.pathogen: None (Plant foliage is physiologically intact and disease-free)
Healthy.conditions: Balanced soil moisture (60–70% field capacity), optimal ambient temperatures (20–30°C), and adequate airflow.
Healthy.symptoms: Uniform green leaf blade without necrotic spots, fungal mycelium, chlorotic halos, or curling.
immediate_action: Maintain regular weekly field scouting throughout vegetative and reproductive stages.
Ensure balanced NPK soil fertilization and avoid excessive vegetative nitrogen.
Monitor canopy humidity and record baseline health photographs.
chemical_control: Preventive bio-fungicide seed treatments can be planned for the subsequent planting cycle.
cultural_management: Maintain certified disease-free seed selection.
Practice 2- to 3-year crop rotation with non-host crops such as maize or sorghum.
Ensure clean field drainage to prevent localized waterlogging.
Healthy.loss_minimization: Document health baseline to benchmark subsequent growth phases.

Soybean rust.conditions: High relative humidity (>90%) with prolonged leaf wetness (6–10 hours) and temperatures between 18°C and 28°C.
Soybean rust.symptoms: Tiny, raised tan to reddish-brown pustules (uredinia) primarily on the underside of lower canopy leaves, progressing to rapid premature defoliation.
immediate_action: Immediately flag infected field sectors and calculate infected leaf percentage.
Scout surrounding rows and lower canopy layers within a 50-meter radius.
Halt all overhead sprinkler irrigation to minimize canopy moisture duration.
chemical_control: Triazole fungicides (e.g., Tebuconazole, Flutriafol, or Difenoconazole) at early symptom onset.
Strobilurin + Triazole premixes (e.g., Azoxystrobin + Difenoconazole or Pyraclostrobin + Fluxapyroxad).
Rotate FRAC groups (FRAC 3 and FRAC 11) to prevent fungicide resistance.
cultural_management: Plant early-maturing, rust-tolerant soybean cultivars.
Adopt wider row spacing (45–50 cm) to facilitate canopy aeration and reduce humidity.
Eradicate alternative legume weed hosts along field perimeters.
Soybean rust.loss_minimization: Apply targeted spray within 48–72 hours of initial detection to prevent yield losses of up to 60–80%.

Frogeye leaf spot.conditions: Warm (25–30°C) and humid conditions with frequent rainfall or heavy morning dew.
Frogeye leaf spot.symptoms: Small, circular to angular spots with light gray/tan centers bordered by narrow, dark reddish-brown margins on upper leaf surfaces.
immediate_action: Examine upper and middle canopy leaves for characteristic circular lesions.
Assess disease incidence before R3 (pod initiation) growth stage.
Collect and isolate representative symptomatic foliage for laboratory verification.
chemical_control: Succinate dehydrogenase inhibitors (SDHI, FRAC 7) combined with DMI triazoles.
Avoid single-site QoI (Strobilurin) applications due to widespread Cercospora sojina QoI resistance.
cultural_management: Deep tillage of infected soybean residue post-harvest to accelerate decomposition.
Rotate with non-host crops like corn or cotton for at least 2 seasons.
Plant resistant soybean varieties with Rcs genes (Rcs1, Rcs2, Rcs3).
Frogeye leaf spot.loss_minimization: Target fungicide applications between R3 (beginning pod) and R5 (beginning seed) if lesions are active.

Bacterial blight.conditions: Cool (20–25°C), wet weather with stormy winds or hail that create micro-wounds in leaf tissue.
Bacterial blight.symptoms: Small, angular water-soaked spots that turn dark brown to black, typically surrounded by distinctive chlorotic (yellow) halos. Lesion centers may drop out.
immediate_action: Strictly prohibit machinery and personnel entry into wet fields to prevent bacterial dispersal.
Avoid foliar nitrogen or mechanical cultivating that could inflict leaf wounds.
Monitor weather forecasts for prolonged cold, overcast spells.
chemical_control: Copper-based bactericides (Copper hydroxide / Copper oxychloride) can provide preventive suppression.
Antibiotics are generally not recommended or approved for field-scale broad-acre use.
cultural_management: Use certified disease-free, high-vigor seed lots.
Incorporate crop residues cleanly into the soil after harvest.
Avoid sprinkler irrigation during early vegetative leaf expansion.
Bacterial blight.loss_minimization: Hot, dry weather (>30°C) naturally suppresses bacterial blight progression.

Downy mildew.conditions: Moderate temperatures (20–22°C) combined with high relative humidity (>85%) and heavy night dew.
Downy mildew.symptoms: Pale green to bright yellow spots on upper leaf surfaces, with corresponding fuzzy, grayish-purple downy fungal tufts on the lower leaf surface.
immediate_action: Inspect lower leaf surfaces early in the morning before dew evaporates.
Check young trifoliates for systemic chlorotic mottling.
Improve air drainage by trimming border weeds and obstacles.
chemical_control: Foliar fungicides containing Mancozeb, Chlorothalonil, or Mefenoxam in severe seed production crops.
Fungicide seed treatment with Metalaxyl/Mefenoxam to prevent seedling systemic infection.
cultural_management: Plow under infected crop residue thoroughly after harvest.
Select resistant soybean cultivars with Rpm genes.
Adopt minimum 1-year rotation away from soybean.
Downy mildew.loss_minimization: Disease rarely causes major economic yield loss on commercial grain unless defoliation exceeds 25%.

Septoria brown spot.conditions: Warm (25–28°C), wet weather with rain splash transporting fungal spores upward through the canopy.
Septoria brown spot.symptoms: Irregular, dark brown lesions on unifoliate and lower trifoliate leaves, coalescing into necrotic patches with surrounding chlorosis and premature leaf drop.
immediate_action: Track whether lesions are restricted to lower canopy or ascending toward the middle third.
Sample lower leaves to confirm absence of rust pustules.
Evaluate canopy closure and ground residue cover.
chemical_control: Triazoles (Prothioconazole, Tebuconazole) applied at R3 growth stage if disease ascends to middle canopy.
Broad-spectrum protective multi-site fungicides (Chlorothalonil) where permitted.
cultural_management: Utilize no-till or reduced-till residue management combined with strict 2-year rotation.
Plant certified fungicide-treated seed.
Optimize planting density to promote rapid lower-canopy drying.
Septoria brown spot.loss_minimization: Treatment is only economically justified if disease advances past the lower third of the canopy before pod fill.

Unknown.conditions: Suboptimal image lighting, out-of-focus capture, or rare physiological disorder (e.g. nutrient deficiency, sunburn, herbicide drift).
Unknown.symptoms: Atypical foliar discoloration, mechanical tearing, or non-diagnostic spots.
immediate_action: Retake a high-resolution, clear photograph in natural daylight without direct lens glare.
Ensure only a single leaf blade is centered in the frame.
Contact your local agricultural extension service or university plant diagnostic clinic.
chemical_control: Do NOT apply broad-spectrum fungicides without confirmed visual or lab diagnosis.
cultural_management: Inspect soil pH, moisture levels, and recent fertilizer/herbicide spray history.
Isolate suspected plants if viral transmission is suspected.
Unknown.loss_minimization: Log coordinates and observe symptoms over a 48-hour period.
